page.layout: Top: two circular portrait medallions with inscriptions around their rims, side by side (left: PTOLOMAEVS, right: ELEAZARVS). Below them: one column of running text, two paragraphs. Below the text: a fleuron ornament (not transcribed). No margin notes, no footnote lines.

main_text.l: PTOLOMAEVS
ELEAZARVS[?]
PTOLOMAEVS Philadelphus, superioris Ptolomæi
filius iunior, successit patri in regno Ægypti, anno mundi
3680. ante Christum natum 282. hic Stratonis discipulus doc-
tissimus fuit:Bibliothecam insignem parauit Alexandriæ. Iu-
dæos qui in Ægypto erant, liberos esse permisit, & vasa Eleaza-
ro summo sacerdoti Ierosolymorum, votiua transmittens, di-
uinas scripturas in Græcam linguam per septuaginta interpre-
tes verti curauit. Huius frater maior natu, qui Seleucum vita
regnoque Macedoniæ priuauerat, amicitiam, pacemque ac
concordiam per epistolas deprecatur, professus deponere se
offensam erepti paterni regni, neque amplius à fratre quæsitu-
rum quod honestius à paterno hoste percepisset. Eutr.lib.2.
Iusti.lib.17.D.Epipha.in lib.de ponde. & mensuris.Iose. lib.Anti-
qui.12.cap.2. Titus Liu.Deca.5.lib.4.&5.
ELEAZARVS, patri Oniæ, cognominato iusto, succes-
sit in pontificatu Iudæorum, anno mundi 3691. ante Christum
natum 271. Ad hunc scripsit Ptolemæus Philadelphus, hic
quoque ad illum: extant utriusque epistolæ apud Iosephum
lib.Antiquit.12.cap.2. Misit hic ad Ptolemæum libros Mosaicæ
legis, atque ex unaquaque tribu senos viros interpretes, He-
braicè Græcéque peritissimos. Consulito D.Augustin.[?]lib.de ci-
uit.Dei 18.cap.42.

page.notes: Medallion inscriptions: the first letter of the right-hand medallion (read as E) is doubtful and the inscription is partly obscured by the portrait; marked [?]. Printed numbers copied as they stand (3680, 282, 3691, 271). The name after "D." in the second paragraph is hard to read on the scan (printed long s/ligature); read as Augustin with [?]. Printed spacing and the colon in "fuit:Bibliothecam" kept as printed. Page number 139 printed at the top right, running head PARS PRIMA. at the top centre.
